idiom_name: struct + impl with smart constructors and enums for alternatives
implementation_notes: Rust keeps the data+behaviour binding (struct and impl) but not the classic mutable shared object graph: fields are private to the module, constructors are smart (OrderId::new(raw) -> Result<Self, _>) so invalid values cannot be constructed, and invariants are validated once at the boundary instead of re-checked everywhere - the 'parse, don't validate' discipline. Identity-bearing aggregates are owned in one place and transitions take &mut self; value objects are newtypes over primitives; alternatives that a Java model would express through subclasses become enums matched exhaustively. The classic mutable entity graph is not idiomatic here because ownership and borrowing reject shared mutable aliasing.
pitfalls: Rust privacy is per module, not per type: sibling items in the same module can bypass invariants - keep the model module small and construction in smart constructors.
Modelling aggregates as Rc<RefCell<...>> to mimic shared mutable entities fights the borrow checker; hold one owner, pass &mut, or reference other aggregates by id.
Deriving PartialEq or Clone on identity-bearing types gives them value semantics; implement equality by id and clone deliberately.
